A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 20-page versions of the same HAF-RM study. Their main sections, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original reward-model accuracy, mixed-data and distribution-shift evaluations, best-of-N selection, RLHF experiments, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results and reports revised downstream results in Table 11 and the RLHF plot.

M1.justification: Both versions use a shared transformer with reward and policy heads, combining the reward-ranking loss with auxiliary DPO loss. The new training diagram illustrates this existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both use Helpful, Harmless, Beaver Safe, Alpaca Human Pref, and Chatbot Arena, plus RewardBench for external evaluation. Mixed-data, OOD transfer, best-of-N, and RLHF task coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 11 removes the Phi-2 DPO and Mistral DPO rows, leaving HAF and the standard reward-model baseline. DPO remains in the main comparisons, including Table 4 and the best-of-N win-rate figures.

E3.justification: Appendix A substantially revises reported PPO settings: batch size 16 to 4, maximum new tokens 256 to 128, learning rate 2e-5 to 1e-6, maximum episodes 100,000 to 20,000, and top_p 0.9 to 0.8. Table 5 changes precision from fp16 to bf16. Appendix F changes the ranking judge from GPT-4-turbo-2024-04-09 to GPT-3.5-turbo, although Section 4.2.1 still specifies GPT-4-turbo. These are reported protocol changes; rerunning is not established.

E4.justification: The policy-loss-ratio sweep, mixed/OOD evaluations, model-consistency analysis, and perplexity-correlation analysis remain. The appendix ablation plot is relocated and renumbered, with its analytical content retained.

E5.justification: Both retain global random seed 0 and the same Pearson correlations and significance reporting in Table 7. Neither introduces additional repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Downstream results are substantially revised. Table 11 replaces most retained recalls and removes DPO results; for example, Mistral HAF's AHP top-1/top-2 values change from 22.86/41.95 to 17.42/31.22. The Chat RLHF trajectory also changes between v3 Figure 5 and v4 Figure 6. These are revised reported outcomes, with comparability limited by changed settings and judge descriptions. Main Tables 2–4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and Appendices C–D retain the same definitions, loss derivations, assumptions, and mathematical inequalities. Their relocation does not change the mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contribution: hybrid token-level and sequence-level supervision improves reward-model training. The shortened introduction preserves the claim's meaning and scope.

C2.justification: The explanations involving shared preferences, policy-loss regularization, DPO fitting behavior, and differing Chat/Safety outcomes remain. The stated limitation concerning combining policy-head and reward-head outputs is unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially rewrites reproducibility information: LLaMA-Factory becomes TRL, and PPO hardware, score normalization/clipping, checkpoint selection, temperature, and generation penalties are newly specified. Conversely, the learning-rate/batch-size search ranges are removed, and reward-model learning-rate assignments become less explicit about backbone and DPO configurations. The code-access statement remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Yue et al. (2024), 'Synergistic multi-agent framework with trajectory learning for knowledge-intensive tasks,' to the related-work discussion and references. The broader positioning of HAF-RM remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 shortens the introduction, DPO description, and conventional-training explanation in related work. It also corrects the RLHF reference from 'Table 5' to 'Figure 6.' Section and appendix organization is otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is simplified and moved to the first page, and a new Figure 2 illustrates training. Win-rate plots are restyled, the RLHF vertical axis changes from 'Accuracy' to 'Win Rates,' the existing ablation figure moves, and Table 11 contracts from six rows to four. Most displays retain their structure.

improvement.justification: Clearer diagrams and additional PPO details help, but v4 introduces unresolved reporting inconsistencies. Its Table 11 Mistral HAF top-1 recalls average 13.31%, while unchanged Table 4 reports 18.19%; v3's corresponding entries supported that summary. Appendix F now specifies GPT-3.5-turbo for ranking while Section 4.2.1 still specifies GPT-4-turbo. These conflicts, together with removed tuning information, reduce reproducibility and outweigh the limited presentation gains.
